topic: How does streaming work in the OpenAI Responses API?
executiveSummary: Streaming in the OpenAI Responses API allows clients to process the beginning of a model's output while generation continues, rather than waiting for the full response [S1]. It is enabled by setting stream=True in the API request and uses HTTP streaming over server-sent events (SSE) [S1]. The API delivers semantic events, each typed with a predefined schema, some emitted once and others repeating during generation [S1].

details:
By default, the OpenAI API generates the entire model output before sending it in a single HTTP response [S1]. Streaming changes this by letting you process the beginning of the model's output while generation continues [S1]. To enable it, set stream=True in the Responses API request; the API then uses HTTP streaming over server-sent events (SSE) [S1].

The Responses API uses semantic events for streaming, and each streaming event is typed with a predefined schema [S1]. Some events are emitted only once, while others repeat during generation [S1]. For example, response.created is emitted when a response is created [S2], and response.output_item.done carries the final encrypted content of an output item [S2]. The response.compaction.compacting event reports summary output at most once every 30 seconds, though a short compaction may finish without emitting a progress event [S2].

Streaming can also involve WebSocket transport: persistent WebSocket transport with previous_response_id uses WebSocket mode [S1], and a response is described as steered when it stops at a safe output boundary after a WebSocket steer event [S2]. In SDKs, streaming events are typed instances [S1].
